messages:
mira (CS): FYI customer (Acme) just escalated — their rerank endpoint is returning different scores for the exact same payload after last night's model update. They gave a small repro and a few request_ids.
acme-support: here are the two request_ids: req_5f3a2 and req_5f3b9. identical inputs, different top result. no 5xx, just score shifts.
acme-support: sample input (sanitized):
```
{
  \"query\": \"best wireless earbuds\",
  \"candidates\": [\"Brand A model X\", \"Brand B model Y\"],
  \"k\": 5
}
```
mira (CS): they said they double-checked bytes and exact JSON. attached diff shows only a trailing space on one of the candidate strings in the failing case. says it was generated programmatically though.
deploy-bot: model-service: deployed model reranker v2.1.7 to prod at 2026-02-18T02:14:22Z by zhang. canary 10%. no errors reported.
samir (SRE): checking routing and canary. no 500s or rate-limit spikes. batching looks normal. sharing logs for req_5f3a2/5f3b9 now.
samir (SRE): logs show two different tokenization lengths: 12 vs 11 tokens on the candidates list for the identical visible text. suspicious.
eva (ML): tagging in — tokenization difference could explain score drift if KV cache alignment or attention padding changed. did anything touch tokenizer / token-normalization?
zhang (eng): I pushed a tiny normalization tweak in the preprocessing pipeline yesterday to trim duplicated whitespace and normalize unicode on inputs for the reranker to reduce OOV tokens. It was enabled behind a feature flag but might have been globally flipped during the deploy.
eva (ML): that would explain it — trailing space on a candidate would become removed in one path and not another, changing token offsets. reranker is sensitive to small token boundary shifts.
mira (CS): customer insists inputs were identical bytes. could this be a client-side difference vs server-side? they ran same curl twice.
samir (SRE): reproduced locally: by sending JSON with a trailing space inside candidate string we get different tokenization depending on whether content-length header is set and whether nginx does any trimming when content-type charset is present. weird edge-case.
eva (ML): root cause hypothesis: normalization change + subtle upstream encoding/trim behavior in the HTTP stack caused one request to hit preprocessed path (flag on) and the other to hit fast-path (flag off). result: identical human-visible strings got tokenized differently -> score divergence.
zhang (eng): rolling back the normalization flip for the reranker feature flag now. will promote patch to disable at 02:35Z.
deploy-bot: model-service: feature-flag rollback completed at 2026-02-18T02:34:58Z for reranker-normalize. canary -> 100% rollback confirmed.
eva (ML): ran the two saved request payloads through current prod and previous prod simulators — scores match now on the exact bytes. looks resolved.
mira (CS): told Acme we'll rollback and follow up with root cause. they're asking for a short incident note and why same inputs changed.
liz (PM): can we get a one-paragraph explainer I can send to the customer + an internal follow-up checklist? include repro steps and mitigation.
eva (ML): 1) summary: normalization flag flip caused tokenization differences for inputs with subtle whitespace/unicode variants; 2) repro: curl two payloads (one with trailing space) to /v1/rerank with content-type application/json; observe token counts and score delta; 3) impact: small number of rerank requests for customers with programmatic string construction; 4) fix: rolled back normalization flag; scheduled PR to harden preprocessing deterministic behavior and add tests; 5) follow-up: add input-identity header check and extra logging for tokenization diffs.
mira (CS): copying this to the customer with ETA for formal RCA. thanks all :thumbsup:
acme-support: thanks, please cc me on the note. appreciated the quick turnaround.
